historicalReferences: This layout might be quicker, but the ghosts of Monza's past still linger – the great battles, the dramatic finishes, the legends forged here.
Even on the Biassono configuration, the names of Ascari, Fangio, and Clark echo around this circuit. Their spirit lives on in every driver who pushes the limit here.
Think back to 1971, and Peter Gethin's incredible win. The slipstreaming battles were legendary, a testament to Monza's high-speed nature.
Senna's battles here in the late 80s and early 90s are etched in the memory, his determination and skill shining through on this challenging circuit.
While this layout bypasses some iconic corners, it still holds its place in Monza's history, offering a different kind of challenge to the drivers.
Remember the incredible finish in 2000, when Michael Schumacher secured victory amidst a sea of red? Moments like that define Monza's magic.
The Monza circuit, in all its forms, has witnessed countless acts of bravery and skill. This year we hope to add another chapter to that story.
Even on the shorter layout, Monza has provided plenty of dramatic moments. The quick nature of the track can lead to incredibly close racing.
Think of the names that have conquered Monza: Schumacher, Hamilton, Alonso. They've all had to tame this beast to achieve glory.
The history of Monza is intertwined with the history of motorsport itself. This Biassono layout is a part of that ongoing legacy.
cornerCallouts: The run down to the first chicane is crucial. Braking late and carrying speed is key, but too much and you'll be running wide.
The Rettifilo chicane demands precision. It's a prime overtaking spot, but also a place where races can be won or lost.
Negotiating Curva Grande at speed is a real test of courage, demanding absolute commitment from the drivers.
The Della Roggia chicane follows quickly after Curva Grande, requiring drivers to scrub speed rapidly.
Ascari presents a real challenge. It's a fast, flowing sequence of corners that rewards bravery and precision.
The Lesmo corners are crucial for maintaining momentum. Get it wrong here, and you'll lose valuable time on the run to the Parabolica.
The Parabolica is still a key corner, even on this layout. A good exit is essential for maximizing speed down the start/finish straight.
The start/finish straight: an opportunity to breathe before diving into the Rettifilo chicane again.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this short, sharp Monza layout. Managing the rubber through the corners will be crucial.
With a lap length of just 3.8 kilometers, the pit window is going to be tight. Timing the stops perfectly will be essential.
Fuel consumption will be a concern, but the shorter lap length might allow for a slightly more aggressive engine mode.
The slipstream will be incredibly powerful on this layout. Expect to see plenty of overtaking opportunities throughout the race.
Teams will be carefully monitoring the weather. A sudden shower could throw the entire strategy out the window.
The undercut could be particularly effective here. Gaining track position with a well-timed pit stop could be a game-changer.
With fewer high-speed corners than the full layout, teams might experiment with slightly different aerodynamic configurations.
The balance between straight-line speed and cornering grip will be crucial. Finding the right compromise will be key to success.

The forecast suggests a stable afternoon, which means we should be in for a dry and exciting race at Monza.
